note: Triennial election of the Clogher rural district councillors, 1930. Fifteen divisions were settled at the nominations (Ulster Herald, 26 April 1930, p. 5); the one possible contest, Ballygawley, ended with R. J. Campbell's withdrawal (Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15). Errigal had no nominations; its retiring member, Charles M'Girr, was deemed re-elected (see the division's note). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 4 June 1930. division inferred from the 1 June 1927 return (Charles M'Girr); the Ulster Herald, 28 June 1930, p. 9 names the member as the representative for Errigal on the council at his death in June 1930, after the election day. No nomination was received for Errigal (Ulster Herald, 26 April 1930, p. 5), so the retiring member was deemed re-elected. He died in June 1930 (Ulster Herald, 21 June 1930, p. 4), and Mr. Patrick M'Kelvey was co-opted in his room in August 1930 (Ulster Herald, 16 August 1930, p. 2); that co-option is not an election. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
